content: 1. Demeclocycline Dosage: The recommended oral dose is 2 mg/kg/day, divided into two or three doses (BID/TID). Alternatively, a dose of 300 mg/m²/day can be used, also divided into two or three doses. 2. Contraindications and Serious Interactions: Acitretin and Tetracyclines: Isotretinoin: This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of pseudotumor cerebri (benign intracranial hypertension). Cholera Vaccine: Avoid co-administration with systemic antibiotics like demeclocycline, as they may inactivate the vaccine strain. Wait at least 14 days after completing antibiotics before administering the vaccine. BCG Vaccine (Live): Contraindicated due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is complete. Typhoid Vaccine (Live): Similarly contraindicated; wait until antibiotic treatment is finished before administering live bacterial vaccines. Strontium Ranelate: This combination is contraindicated as it reduces demeclocycline absorption. Suspend strontium ranelate during antibiotic therapy. 3. Serious Interactions Requiring Alternatives: Aluminum Hydroxide, Calcium Salts (e.g., Calcium Acetate, Calcium Carbonate, Calcium Chloride, Calcium Citrate, Calcium Gluconate): These reduce demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate administration by at least 2 hours or use alternative drugs. Iron Supplements (e.g., Carbonyl Iron, Ferrous Fumarate, Ferrous Gluconate, Ferrous Sulfate): These also reduce demeclocycline absorption. Administer demeclocycline 2 hours before or several hours after iron supplements. Magnesium Salts (e.g., Magnesium Chloride, Magnesium Citrate, Magnesium Hydroxide, Magnesium Oxide, Magnesium Sulfate): These decrease demeclocycline levels by forming insoluble complexes. Administer magnesium 2 hours before or 4 hours after demeclocycline. Bismuth Subsalicylate: Reduces demeclocycline absorption. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Sucralfate: Reduces demeclocycline absorption. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cholestyramine and Colestipol: These reduce demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. Sodium Bicarbonate and Sodium Citrate: These reduce demeclocycline absorption. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. Multivalent Cation-Containing Products (e.g., Lanthanum Carbonate, Tripotassium Dicitratobismuthate): These reduce demeclocycline bioavailability. Administer demeclocycline at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these agents. 4. Interactions with Antibiotics: Penicillins (e.g., Amoxicillin, Ampicillin, Penicillin G, Penicillin VK): Demeclocycline may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins, reducing their therapeutic effects. Avoid or monitor closely. Cephalosporins (e.g., Cefdinir, Cefditoren, Cefoxitin, Cefpodoxime, Ceftriaxone, Cefuroxime): Demeclocycline may reduce their effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Piperacillin: Similar antagonism is observed; monitor closely. 5. Interactions with Retinoids and Photosensitizing Agents: Aminolevulinic Acid (Oral and Topical): Co-administration increases phototoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Tretinoin (Oral and Topical): Increases phototoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Porfimer and Verteporfin: These enhance photosensitivity when combined with demeclocycline. Use caution and monitor closely. Methoxsalen: Additive phototoxic effects are observed. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Interactions with Hormonal Contraceptives: Conjugated Estrogens, Ethinyl Estradiol, Estradiol, Levonorgestrel, Mestranol, Estropipate: Demeclocycline may reduce their effectiveness by altering intestinal flora. While the risk of contraceptive failure is low, caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Interactions with Anticoagulants and Antithrombotic Agents: Warfarin: Demeclocycline may increase its effects. Use caution and monitor closely. Heparin, Enoxaparin, Dalteparin, Fondaparinux, Bivalirudin, Bemiparin: Demeclocycline may enhance their effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Monitor closely. 8. Interactions with Vitamins and Nutritional Supplements: Biotin, Thiamine, Niacin, Pantothenic Acid, Pyridoxine: Demeclocycline may reduce their levels by altering intestinal flora. Monitor closely. Rose Hips: Demeclocycline increases elimination of rose hips, reducing their levels. Monitor closely. 9. Other Notable Interactions: Methotrexate: Demeclocycline may increase methotrexate levels by decreasing its elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. Digoxin: Demeclocycline may increase digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora. Use caution and monitor closely. Mipomersen: Both drugs may increase hepatic enzyme levels. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely. 10. Minor Interactions: Demeclocycline may have minor or unknown significance interactions with drugs like antithrombin alfa, argatroban, balsalazide, and protamine. Monitor closely if co-administered. In summary, demeclocycline has numerous interactions with other drugs, particularly those affecting gastrointestinal absorption, photosensitivity, and hormonal contraceptives. Careful monitoring, dose adjustments, or alternative therapies may be required in many cases.
